title: Dynamical Polarization from Hidden Spin and Orbital Textures in p-Wave Magnets
authors: Yantao Li, Jacob Linder, Pavlo Sukhachov
abstract: Period-averaged descriptions often miss essential features of driven quantum matter. We show that the micromotion of an optically driven $p$-wave magnet unveils a hidden net spin polarization, absent from both the equilibrium and period-averaged spin textures, which remain odd in momentum. This spin polarization oscillates at the drive frequency and is resonantly enhanced at the interband gap set by nonrelativistic exchange splitting. The drive further activates an orbital angular momentum governed by interband quantum geometry. While its linear response remains momentum-odd, nonlinear rectification yields a static, momentum-even orbital polarization for suitably oriented driving fields. These results establish $p$-wave magnets as a source of resonant ac spin and rectified dc orbital polarization: effects invisible to any period-averaged treatment.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates dynamical spin and orbital polarizations in p-wave magnets under periodic driving. It shows that the time-averaged picture fails to capture key physics, demonstrating that driving converts hidden momentum-odd textures into measurable ac spin and static dc orbital responses. The methodology combines Floquet theory with Kubo response calculations.
main_problem: The study addresses how periodic driving can reveal essential dynamical polarization effects (spin and orbital) in p-wave magnets that are entirely missed by standard period-averaged descriptions.
main_result: Periodic driving generates a measurable, static, momentum-even orbital polarization and an oscillating ac spin polarization, both of which originate from hidden, momentum-odd textures invisible to time-averaging.
method: The analysis employs Floquet theory combined with the Kubo linear response formalism to calculate time-dependent expectation values for spin and orbital angular momenta.
model_or_system: The system is a p-wave magnet described by an effective Hamiltonian, analyzed using continuum models incorporating exchange coupling ($J_{sd}$) and subjected to periodic driving fields (e.g., electric field $E(t)$).
key_observables: Spin polarization ($\langle\langle \hat{S} angleangle$), Orbital Angular Momentum ($\langle\langle \hat{L} angleangle$), Dynamical Spin Edelstein Response ($\chi^{(S)}$), and Rectified Orbital Polarization ($\chi^{(L),(2)}$).
important_parameters: The resonant enhancement occurs near the interband gap set by nonrelativistic exchange splitting, and the analysis depends on the drive frequency $\omega$.
main_assumptions: Key approximations include using the Floquet formalism for time evolution and employing the relaxation time approximation in the density matrix equations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics of light-induced oscillating spin polarization and rectified orbital angular momentum, comparing period-averaged versus instantaneous texture components for both spin and orbital moments.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the Floquet formalism to calculating time-dependent expectation values. It then applies Kubo linear response theory to derive the dynamical spin Edelstein effect (linear response) and subsequently calculates second-order terms to find the rectified, static orbital polarization.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete theoretical framework for understanding how non-equilibrium driving can unlock novel, measurable quantum responses in magnetic materials, which is crucial for designing advanced spintronic devices.
